summary: Unpair a paired device from Settings, behind a confirmation that names the device and says the phone must pair again with a new PIN. First production caller of PairedClientRegistry.UnregisterClient, behind its own narrow IPairedDeviceRevoker. Clears FIVE stores - review found the file-transfer trust grant, which comes back as privilege rather than a label because that store prunes only for unpaired clients. Every teardown runs even when an earlier one throws (the original credential-first rationale was backwards: the registry is the first call and the only one that propagates), failures rethrown as AggregateException and reported by the command. Review PASS after two HIGHs fixed. Filed RemEx-6nkht (live session survives unpair) and RemEx-pynli (failed credential write brings the pairing back on restart). verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2098/2099; five injections all bit, one of which caught an inert guard of mine that asked the self-pruning trust API instead of the file on disk.

Unpairing a device now ends its live connections, not just future ones. IsClientPaired is consulted only when a connection is established, so a phone already mirroring the desktop kept mirroring it after being unpaired. Three channels, three owners: ClientSessionRegistry aborts every matching control socket (all of them, not Find's newest; IdentityProven-filtered so a loopback claimant cannot be used to cut the PC's own connection), DesktopSessionRegistry cancels the stream via its existing drain contract, TransferSessionManager aborts the file socket and lets RunChannelAsync's own finally suspend partials. PairedDeviceDisconnector hops off the caller's thread first, because otherwise the entire capture teardown unwound on the Avalonia dispatcher under a Settings button. Three review rounds, first two FAIL: round 1 found the UI-thread unwind, round 2 found that the fix for it had no guard (deleting the Task.Run left the suite green) plus two more inert guards and two throwing-logger escape routes, round 3 found CancelAsync had become load-bearing for the drain budget while its comment still called it a style choice. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2113/2114; eight injections all bit.

A failed unpair now says whether the pairing will come back. UnregisterClient removes from memory then persists, so a failed write leaves the device unpaired for this run and untouched on disk - back on the next start. PairedDeviceRevocationException carries PairingMayReturn, set from whether the CREDENTIAL teardown failed rather than any failure, and the Settings command picks its wording from it. Review also caught that the new exception's Message is a constant where AggregateException's appended its inners, so the toast had silently lost the actual reason and was showing untranslated English in eight locales; Reason now joins the failures. Divergence test uses a per-OS injection (read-only file on Windows, write bit off the directory on Unix - rename consults the directory, not the target) and a probe that fails loudly under root rather than skipping. Three review rounds, first two FAIL: round 2 found the lost reason and that my guard had fabricated the Message it was testing; round 3 found every remaining assertion was direction-blind and would ship a swapped ternary green. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2116/2117; five injections all bit.

Item 3 of RemEx-7ykyn: the QR and the PIN are one act behind one button. They were always one pairing session - GenerateQrCodeAsync starts it and encodes that PIN - but sat behind two buttons opening two panels. Collapsed to one button per host, the panel refresh renews both, plate 180->260, and the pairing block hoisted above the image work so a rendering failure cannot cost the PIN. Review returned FAIL with three HIGHs, all fixed: collapsing the buttons had deleted the surface's only failure feedback and left a pin=null QR being drawn; UriFormatException escaped the command and would kill the app on the now-sole pairing path; and the sixteenth inert guard - RevealPinAlongsideTheCode has two call sites and emptying the method killed both, so deleting only the standalone one (the normal installed shape) left the suite green. The fifteenth was found earlier in the same diff by injection. Fixes not re-reviewed. Item 4 (NotificationRouter feedback) and three review follow-ups recorded on the bead. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2123/2124.

Item 4 completes RemEx-7ykyn. Pairing failures now announce through NotificationService/NotificationRouter as Problem, so they reach a tray balloon when the window is hidden - StatusText alone was not feedback in an app that closes to the tray. The PIN is never announced, only failures, and a test holds that. Review returned FAIL with two HIGHs that were the same mistake on both sides: the fallback message was gated on string.IsNullOrEmpty(StatusText), which can never be true since StatusText is initialised to Disconnected, so pressing pair with no service attached produced total silence - and the assertion covering it used NotBeEmpty, which passes on a view model that never ran. Making the assertion exact immediately caught a third defect: the no-PIN check sat below the address and certificate lookups whose catch blocks overwrote StatusText, so a host that produced no PIN reported a QR failure instead. Fixes not re-reviewed. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2126/2127.

P1 bug, NOT completed. Diagnosis only, no code changed. Ruled out suspect 3 by tracing callers: the file-channel teardown I added in RemEx-6nkht is reachable only from the Settings unpair button behind a confirmation, so it cannot cut a still-paired device's channel. Identified a concrete mechanism for suspect 2: /ws/files is gated on protocolVersion>=3 and refuses v2 peers outright, which reproduces the exact symptom (control channel fine, both transfer directions missing at the _channels lookup) and leaves a named rejection line in the host log that distinguishes it from suspect 1 in one read. Suspect 1 stays open: the channel is keyed on the query-string clientId while the download path looks up the control socket's id, Ordinal. Symptom 1 is a product decision for Connor (option (a), split by consent KIND, is the only one meeting the stated expectation without re-breaking RemEx-mneb) and symptom 2 needs device logs against the installed exe. Blocked on both.

HandleReady resolved a pending host-initiated push for whoever answered, with no owner check - the fifth transfer-id entry point, left out of RemEx-juas because IsForeignTransfer cannot answer for a pending push (no session, no manifest yet). The owner had to be recorded rather than derived: PushFileAsync had the client id in hand and discarded it. _pendingReady now carries PendingPush(ClientId, Ready) and HandleReady refuses a mismatch in the shape of its siblings. Injection found the eighteenth inert guard inside this diff - asserting push.IsCompleted is false is true either way because PushFileAsync keeps working after its wait resolves - replaced with a capturing logger on the refusal itself; review then found the nineteenth, a tail Assert.False(await push) that a 30s deadline satisfies just as well, now bounded. Review PASS. Filed a P4 for compare-and-remove, which this change made a one-liner. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2129/2130.

App hand-built the dashboard-layout path from SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData for its pre-window theme read, bypassing the RemexDataPaths redirect that RemEx-ln0k introduced. The defect is the second resolver rather than a wrong path: both pointed at the same file in production, so a test that redirected the service still had App reading and writing the developer's own saved dashboard. DefaultFilePath is now internal and App uses it; the ForTests alias is deleted and the redirection test pins the real member, since an alias can be asserted while production reads something else. Added an exact-set guard over remex.desktop for files that still resolve the per-user directory themselves - exact rather than a ceiling, so it fails on a new offender AND on a fixed one left in the list. It named two stragglers: RemexSavefileService (RemEx-mz9f) and FileTransferRootSettingsService, newly filed as RemEx-dnn2q. Review skipped as mechanical, recorded in the trailer. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2130/2131.

The fifth per-user store, missed by RemEx-ln0k's list of four: RemexSavefileService resolved BackupsDirectory from SpecialFolder in its constructor and the auto-snapshot path writes there, so it was one test away from writing real snapshots into the developer's own backups folder. Routed through RemexDataPaths.PerUserDirectory. The new assertion CONSTRUCTS the service, because the defect was in the constructor - pinning a static default would not have covered it. The exact-set guard added under RemEx-mzbn worked exactly as intended: RemexSavefileService had to come off its known-stragglers list as part of this change, which a no-more-than-N ceiling would have let rot into a stale entry vouching for a fix nobody made. One straggler left, RemEx-dnn2q. Review skipped as mechanical, recorded in the trailer. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2131/2132; injection AC fails 2 of 11 - the behavioural assertion and the set guard independently.

A false positive from the guard I added under RemEx-mzbn, and the iteration went to fixing the guard rather than the code. FileTransferRootSettingsService passes the legacy folder INTO RemexDataPaths.ResolveDirectory, which consults HostStateDirectoryOverride before the folder it was given, so the redirect is honoured - the SpecialFolder mention is the off-Windows fallback argument. The guard matched the token instead of the shape, and its only remedy was adding a name to an allowlist, which is how a list that can absorb a false positive comes to absorb a real one. Rule is now: naming the folder is fine, using it without RemexDataPaths is not - so there is no allowlist left. Making it stricter surfaced two more faults in it: it split on Environment.NewLine in a repo with mixed CRLF/LF, so on an LF file the whole file was one line, the comment filter never applied, and it flagged DashboardLayoutService for the doc comment describing the fix; and its name still claimed an allowlist. Both injections it exists for still bite. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2131/2132.

Four host-state stores wrote straight over their live file. Not the one-line adoption the bead expected: two are async, so a sync call would block the caller and removing their only await is a compile error here - added RemexDataPaths.WriteAllTextAtomicAsync rather than inlining the staging rule at those call sites, since inlining it is how a per-write temp name becomes a fixed one again. The two bodies stay duplicated (sharing them means blocking on a task or a delegate indirection on a NativeAOT path) but the staging NAME now has one definition in StagingPathFor, which is the part whose divergence would reintroduce RemEx-kow1. Review PASS with two MEDIUMs, both the same shape as the guard unwound two commits ago: StagingFiles() globbed *.tmp so every no-debris assertion was blind to exactly the drift the duplication creates, and the adoption theory banned the File.WriteAllText string inside a 1300-line file-writing class where the next correct write would have failed it. Both retargeted - enumerate everything but the store, and match each store's own path variable. verify.ps1 FULL scope PASS 2138/2139; three injections all bit, one of them invisible before the StagingFiles fix.

A kill -9 between staging and rename leaves the staging file, and per-write names removed the collision that used to make that self-limiting. For paired_clients.json each orphan is a full copy of the reconnect secrets carrying the INHERITED ProgramData ACL, since RestrictStorePermissions only runs on the final path. Added RemexDataPaths.SweepStagingOrphans, age-bounded because deleting a file a concurrent writer holds fails on Windows but SUCCEEDS on Linux and breaks that writer's rename. Wired into PairedClientRegistry.LoadFromDisk before the existence check. Review FAIL with one HIGH: my join test created the store first, so File.Exists was true and moving the sweep below the early return left it green - while the store-absent case is exactly what a killed first write produces. Also found the production threshold constant was on no test path (the fresh-file test restated the literal through the internal seam) and that the store-itself assertion was tautological under an anchored glob. All fixed; fixes not re-reviewed. Filed RemEx-njzcx for the other eight stores, carrying the review's correction that CertificateService does NOT have the security half - it ACLs its staging file at creation.

Ported the salvaged security test asserting a paired non-loopback connection cannot inherit another device's full-browse grant by naming its clientId. It looked covered by RemEx-4215's LoopbackIdentityClaimTests and was not: those drive the LOOPBACK gate where identity is never proven and the freeze is at NO identity, while this is the paired path with a different freeze point - misreading that is why the test was dropped when RemEx-9i4b was finished. The bead said to confirm rather than assume its original blocker was gone, so I checked the machine-wide trust file directly: neither fixture id present, mtime 88 minutes old, and NewHost overrides the store with a per-run temp path. Injection AJ (drop the identityProven half of the freeze at PingPongHandler.cs:210) makes the attacker inherit the grant and the test fails, so it is not a test that merely passes. Review skipped as a test-only port, recorded in the trailer. Also picked up and put back down RemEx-7cq0: its own description gates it on the RemEx-w7ei flake recurring, which it has not, and doing it now would spend the fix's diagnostic value. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2144/2145.

The drain-wait timeout message reports the last count the WAIT saw and, separately, what is in the registry now; they differ only in the near-miss case the message exists to name, and that branch had no coverage - the existing test uses a session that never drains, so both numbers agree and a regression re-reading the registry for the headline still passes. It was left uncovered knowingly because standing a near miss up against the live wait is a race on exactly the starved pool the area is about. Took the seam the bead asked for in its smallest form: extracted the message into a pure function of what was observed, so the near miss is a plain unit test with counts handed in and no timing at all. Injection AK (headline re-reads the registry) fails the new test while the pre-existing one passes, which is the asymmetry that made this worth filing. Review skipped as test-only, recorded in the trailer. verify.ps1 -Scope dotnet PASS 2145/2146.

Wired RemexDataPaths.SweepStagingOrphans into all eight remaining atomic-write stores, the important one being file_transfer_trust.json - standing filesystem authorisation whose orphans are ACL-inherited copies. At LOAD not on write, because sweeping on write only collects an orphan if the store is written again and the crashed-first-write case is exactly where it is not; two stores sweep in their constructor instead because their read path is hot. Every test constructs its store with NO store file on disk, which pins the PLACEMENT rather than the call - the lesson from RemEx-jegp's review, where a test that created the store first passed with the sweep moved below the early return. Injection AL points three stores' sweeps at the wrong path and exactly those three theory cases fail, so each case is independently live. Six of eight guarded; DashboardProfileStorageService and FileTransferRootSettingsService have no path seam and are wired but unguarded, filed as RemEx-azh2u (P4, both per-user and non-secret). Note: the commit first cited an invented bead id and was amended before anything else touched it. verify.ps1 FULL scope PASS 2152/2153.

The desktop is a client as well as a host and had the same silence the phone had before RemEx-3qmd: ListVolumesAsync dropped denyReason, so a peer's host refusing without asking anybody produced the flat 'not granted' - true of both outcomes, actionable for only one. Ported the SHAPE natively rather than sharing code, as the bead required: errorMessage wins, then granted, then the reason code, else a plain refusal, with an absent reason meaning a person decided (RemEx-l580's contract). Added VolumesResponseClassifier plus one string x 9 locales.
